title: Moving Beyond the Click: Omnichannel Campaign Planning
summary: Master omnichannel campaign planning by connecting CTV and web placements to build trust, optimise touchpoints, and drive sales beyond the click.
body_markdown:
Consumers do not experience a brand one channel at a time. They move from the living-room screen to a mobile device, from a premium article to a product page, and back again. The next advantage in omnichannel campaign planning is not simply adding more placements. It is designing the sequence between them.


## Why advertising needs a cross-screen plan


When linear TV, connected TV and digital are bought in separate silos, advertisers risk duplicated frequency, fragmented identity and creative that is optimised for a platform rather than a person. Clicks can be a useful signal, but they are not the same as purchase conviction. Trust builds through repeated, relevant encounters in environments where people are paying attention.


***[The Connected Consumer Blueprint, Volume 1](https://view-su2.highspot.com/viewer/a5d9578112c7c62f269404d9521ddcae?source=slack#1)*** , shows why this matters. In research with Censuswide, 31% of UK shoppers say they need four to six separate screen interactions before moving towards purchase. A further 35.4% say that seeing an ad on TV followed by product information on premium news and lifestyle websites gives them the highest confidence to buy; this rises to 45% among Millennials. And 53.9% say they are likely to look up a brand on a companion device after seeing it on a Smart TV home screen.

## The role of CTV in omnichannel advertising


CTV is not just an awareness channel. It can be the first step in a full-funnel omnichannel strategy: capturing shared household attention in the evening, then connecting that exposure to lean-in research on mobile and desktop. The report’s 24-hour attention model shows why media planning should follow human rhythms, not channel ownership.


Three principles make that strategy actionable:


1. **Plan by attention context.** Use CTV for high-impact awareness, then premium open-web environments for consideration and product research.
2. **Unify audience targeting across screens.** A privacy-first household graph can help connect big-screen exposure with personal-device intent, reduce wasteful frequency duplication and make programmatic omnichannel advertising more coherent.
3. **Measure the whole journey.** Set KPIs for awareness, recall, message association and purchase intent alongside qualified site visits and conversions. That is the foundation of credible omnichannel campaign measurement.


Teads’ Omnichannel Grid and Reach & Engage \[BETA\] are designed around this cross-screen handshake: consolidating multi-KPI optimisation so awareness can lead to digital action rather than stopping at the click.
